## Bristol — eight credible candidates

1. **Central Library rhyme and story time — selected for today's campaign.** Wednesday 16 September at 10:45am. Around 20 minutes; free; no booking; ages 0–3; older siblings welcome. Central is marked as all-year. Source: https://www.bristol.gov.uk/residents/libraries-and-archives/services-for-children-and-young-people/baby-bounce-and-rhyme-and-storytime-sessions
2. **Tyntesfield Heritage Open Days.** Free entry 16–20 September, 10am–6pm, last entry 5pm; no booking; everyone welcome. Slopes/loose gravel; mobility shuttle 10am–5pm. Source: https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/bath-bristol/tyntesfield/events/181b773f-1fc7-4a87-8f4b-41c89c2dd4c8
3. **Dyrham Park Heritage Open Days.** Free entry and parking 17–19 September only, 10am–5pm, last entry 4pm; no booking; all ages. House 11:30am; steep and uneven parkland. Source: https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/bath-bristol/dyrham-park/events/94f2b171-9191-4b0e-a234-810e59b3fe3f
4. **Sea Shanty Shout.** Great Eastern Hall, Brunel Square, 19–20 September, noon–6pm. Free, no booking; donations accepted. It is not on the ship. Source: https://www.bristoldockyards.org/whats-on/bristol-sea-shanty-shout
5. **Arnold Art Cart.** Free self-led family making at Arnolfini, Tuesday–Sunday 11am–6pm. Already promoted on 15 September; retained as an indoor weekend option but not selected again. Source: https://arnolfini.org.uk/whatson/arnold-art-cart/
6. **Trinity Community Celebration Day.** Sunday 20 September, 12–4pm; £0–£3 donation; all ages, under-14s with an adult. Workshops, music, nature and craft drop-ins. Accessibility requests by contact. Source: https://www.trinitybristol.org.uk/whats-on/2026/trinitys-community-day-celebration
7. **Docks Heritage Weekend.** M Shed, 19–20 September. Free quiz trail runs 15–20 September; paper-boat and colouring workshop is Saturday. Charges apply to crane visits and boat trips; exact workshop times are not published, so hold from the concise roundup. Source: https://www.bristolmuseums.org.uk/whats-on/m-shed/docks-heritage-weekend/
8. **Free Aardman mini-museum hunt.** Bristol Museum & Art Gallery through 1 November; free detective map and hidden Aardman treasures for all ages. Distinct from the M Shed exhibition that ended 13 September. Source: https://www.bristolmuseums.org.uk/whats-on/bristol-museum-and-art-gallery/mini-museum-hunt-aardman/

Selection covers babies/toddlers, outdoor heritage, music/performance, art/making and a free museum trail across five organisers. Docks Heritage Weekend remains a hold because useful workshop logistics are incomplete.

## Cardiff — eight candidates

1. **St Margaret's Open Doors:** Saturday 19 September 12:30–5:30pm and Sunday 20 September 2–5:30pm; free, no booking; children's quiz trail. Tower ascent is able-bodied adults only; disabled church entry through porch. https://cadw.gov.wales/open-doors-st-margarets-church-roath
2. **Penylan LEGO:** weekly Saturday 10–11am; free drop-in; ages 2+. The recurring page does not explicitly date 19 September, so retain as a confirm-before-travel backup. https://cardiffhubs.co.uk/hub-events/clwb-lego/
3. **National Museum Cardiff:** free general admission Tuesday–Sunday 10am–5pm, galleries close 4:45pm; under-16s with adult; optional free day ticket; parking £6.50. https://museum.wales/cardiff/visit/
4. **Bute Park sculpture hunt:** more than twenty wooden sculptures, including climbable frog and beetle; park page currently shows 7:30am–7pm. Self-led, free ordinary park use. https://bute-park.com/attraction/sculpture-trail/
5. **Insole Court garden tour:** Sunday 20 September, sessions hourly 10am–3pm; free/donations, about 45 minutes, uneven paths; advance tickets only, no walk-ups. Ticket availability and child admission remain unchecked, so hold. https://cadw.gov.wales/open-doors-insole-court
6. **Lisvane and Llanishen Reservoirs:** open 9am–6pm, but an active banner warns of path closures for about eight weeks from 8 September. Do not promise the full circuit or story trail. https://lisvane-llanishen.com/opening-times/
7. **St Mellons youth softball/baseball:** Wednesdays 4:30–5:30pm; free; equipment supplied; ages 9–13, younger on request. The page gives a hub phone number but no explicit drop-in/booking process. https://cardiffhubs.co.uk/hub-events/145799/
8. **Rhydypennau story and rhyme:** weekly Friday 10:30–11:15am; free, no booking; under-5s. https://cardiffhubs.co.uk/hub-events/story-and-rhyme-time-english/

## Birmingham — eight candidates

1. **Brum Transport Fest:** Friday 18 and Saturday 19 September, 11am–5pm; free, no booking; vehicles, museum displays and family activities; all ages; outdoor and wheelchair accessible. Chamberlain Square remains labelled TBC. https://birminghamheritageweek.co.uk/event/brum-transport-festival/
2. **Moor Pool Heritage Festival:** Sunday 20 September, 11am–3pm; free, no booking; crafts, trails, LEGO, sport tasters and brass band. Most of the estate is accessible but some routes have steps/uneven surfaces; side wheelchair entrance to the hall. https://birminghamheritageweek.co.uk/event/moor-pool-heritage-festival/
3. **Make a Mini Museum:** Birmingham Museum & Art Gallery, Sunday 20 September, 11am–3pm; free drop-in; all ages; children supervised by an adult. https://www.birminghammuseums.org.uk/events/marvellous-makers
4. **Helios:** illuminated Sun sculpture at The Exchange; free, no booking; Monday–Saturday 8am–5pm, closed Sunday. https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/the-exchange/events/helios
5. **Explore Blakesley:** Saturday 19 September, grounds 11am–4pm and timed Hall entry 11am–3pm; £5 adult/£3 child; all ages; pre-book essential. https://www.birminghammuseums.org.uk/events/heritage-open-day-and-birmingham-heritage-week-explore-blakesley
6. **Lapworth Museum:** fossils, minerals and Roary the Jurassic predator; free, no booking; September weekday hours 10am–4pm, weekend noon–5pm; pram/wheelchair access and baby change. https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/cultural-attractions/lapworth-museum-of-geology/visit-us
7. **Darlaston rhyme time:** Friday 18 September 10–10:45am; drop-in, preschool. The page still omits a price and it is outside Birmingham city proper, so hold. https://go.walsall.gov.uk/events/rhyme-time-163
8. **Solihull library early-years sessions:** the source lists scheduled rhymetime/storytime but not price and is outside Birmingham city proper. Hold rather than import an old free claim. https://www.solihull.gov.uk/libraries/children-and-young-peoples-library-services
